newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher, but volume light.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher, but volume light.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended higher Tuesday, but volumes were light, and traders were unsure whether the month-long recovery in prices was resuming after last week's downward correction.
"Gold only closed higher because of late fund buying, after spending most of the session lower, but good resistance is seen around $355 in the April contract," FIMAT New York trader John Tyree said.
COMEX April gold closed up $2.00 at $355.00 an ounce, after trading in a $351.60-355.50 range. Estimated total gold futures volume was 30,000 lots.
In the bullion market spot gold ended quoted $353.30/80 compared to the London afternoon fix at $351.95.

"We continue to feel that upside price potential for gold will remain limited until there are significant shifts in sentiment toward supply pressure from central banks and producers, and the favorable economic and political backdrop for paper assets," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.
The Dutch central bank's official gold reserves fell by 1.328 billion guilders to 10.869 billion in the week ended March 10, confirming the Dutch sale of 300 tonnes in January.
But Monday Bundesbank president Tietmeyer reiterated his belief that there would be no more European central bank gold sales for now.
"The close today looked strong but producer selling was seen around $360 and producers may now be lowering their targets again," Mitsui USA bullion dealer, Greg Drury, said.
Producers have also been seen using options strategies to earn premium income around $360, analysts said.

The $27 gold rally in February pushed implied options volatilities back up towards 11 percent, from lows of around 5.5 pct last November, but volatilities are still only back to around the median of the past three years, and well off the three year high near 22 pct, analysts noted.
However, good physical demand from Asia, particularly India, should provide support around $340, analysts said.
"In the absence of fresh incentives it looks as if we are in for a mostly sideways market for a few months," Merrill Lynch analyst Ted Arnold said in a report.
COMEX May silver closed up 1.0 cent at $5.285, after trading a $5.235-5.300 range.
But May silver still looks trapped in a $5.200-5.400 range, analysts said.

"The elastic nature of silver demand from the developing countries, most notably India, and ample physical inventories of silver also suggest limited upside potential above the $5.50 level," Rinehimer said.
NYMEX April platinum closed up $3.10 an ounce at $386.50, after seeing a $384.50-389.00 range.
NYMEX June palladium ended up $6.00 an ounce at $161.25, closing at a new contract high.
A union leader at Russia's Norilsk plant said Tuesday that talks with management had got nowhere ahead of the planned strike on March 27 and April 2.
Some analysts believe Russian stockpiles of platinum are now only about 500,000 ounces, while palladium inventories are about two million ounces.
Russia exported about 1.10 million ounces of platinum in 1996, but only 580,000 ounces came from the Norilsk plant, with the rest drawn from stockpiles, analysts said.
Russia accounts for about 25 percent of world palladium supply and 66 pct of its palladium supply.

Meanwhile, US hedge fund interest in palladium continues, and is seen by some analysts behind the 77 pct rise in US imports of palladium from Russia to 58.5 tonnes in the January-to-November 1996 period.
Swiss imports of Russian palladium also jumped 72 pct to 26.7 tonnes in the year ended December 1996, CRU International noted in a recent report.
Meanwhile, palladium imports to Japan fell 21 pct last year and have since been suspended.
((-Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641 - email: clive.mckeef @ reuters.com))
